message.content:
In a standard Texas Hold’em hand the **maximum number of hearts a single player can hold is five** – that happens when all five community cards are hearts (and the player’s two hole cards are hearts as well, giving them a “five‑heart flush” hand).  

So, the player who ends up with the most hearts in their hand (up to five) is the one with the highest number of hearts in that particular game. If you’re playing a different variant (e.g., Omaha), the theoretical maximum rises (Omaha allows up to nine hearts in total, four in your hand plus five on the board), but the principle is the same: the player with the most hearts in their hand wins that count.
